messages:
maya.k: Hey team — after upgrading our app to @redwood/sdk v0.23.0 our TypeScript client calls to streaming chat are returning 404s. No obvious migration notes in the changelog. Anyone seen this?

alex.support: Sorry to hear that. Can you paste the minimal repro and the exact error body? 404 usually means route name changed or SDK is calling the wrong path.

maya.k: Repro below (TS/node). It used to work on 0.22.x. Now it fails immediately. // stack + response at the end

```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-medium', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hello' }], sessionId: 's-123' });
```

Response (curl'd by the SDK):
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
{ "error": "route_not_found", "route": "/v1/chat/stream" }

stack: Error: Request failed with status code 404
    at createError (...)

alex.support: Ok thanks. Quick questions: 1) Which package exactly (npm ls @redwood/sdk) 2) Are you using the hosted API or dedicated? 3) Can you try a manual curl to /v1/chat.create to see if that route exists?

maya.k: npm ls shows @redwood/sdk@0.23.0. We're on hosted. I just tried curl to /v1/chat.create and it returns 200 and new chat id. So the API still has chat.create but SDK is calling /v1/chat/stream.

alex.support: That points to an SDK->API mapping mismatch. Thanks — I'll escalate if we confirm a breaking rename. In the meantime can you try calling the raw REST endpoint as a short-term workaround? Example:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-medium","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"session":"s-123"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.create
```

maya.k: That works. Note the body property name is session vs sessionId — we used sessionId in SDK earlier. So two issues: wrong route and param rename.

ryan.eng: Looping in runtime team — @sam.eng-ml can you confirm if there was a planned removal of the chat/stream route or param rename in API?

sam.eng-ml: We rolled a change last week standardizing chat RPCs: chat.create is the canonical REST route and sessionId was renamed to session in the API surface. We kept backwards shims for old SDKs but removed the shim for streaming path accidentally in the hosted gateway config. This caused SDKs that still call /v1/chat/stream to get 404s.

ryan.eng: Thanks. So root cause = gateway route cleanup + SDK update that switched client surface to new names. Impact = TS/Node SDK 0.23.0 clients that still call .stream or send sessionId.

alex.support: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) Re-introduce a temporary gateway redirect from /v1/chat/stream -> /v1/chat.create (done as hotfix) 2) Patch SDK to map sessionId -> session and call chat.create in 0.23.1 3) Advise customers to call raw REST or pin to 0.22.x for now.

deploy-bot: Hotfix deployed to gateway (route alias /v1/chat/stream -> /v1/chat.create) in region us-west-2; will propagate to other regions in ~5m.

maya.k: Confirmed — after ~2m my calls started returning 200 again. Thanks! Any ETA on the SDK patch?

sam.eng-ml: We'll cut 0.23.1 today that restores compatibility and adds an explicit migration note. ETA ~ 4 hours. Release will: map sessionId -> session, prefer chat.create, and keep a deprecation warning when sessionId is used. We'll also add unit tests to prevent gateway/SDK drift.

ryan.eng: Action items:
- eng-runtime: add gateway monitoring alert for route alias deletions (sam)
- sdk: publish 0.23.1 with compatibility shim and tests (alex)
- support: notify customers who reported 404s and recommend pin/workaround (ryan)

alex.support: I'll prepare the release notes and a short support KB: "TS SDK 0.23.0: 404 on chat.streaming -> workaround and update path" — include repro and curl snippet.

maya.k: Appreciate the quick turnaround. One last thing — we saw a minor latency spike during the outage (~200ms additional per request) while the hotfix propagated. Not critical but FYI.

sam.eng-ml: Noted. We'll watch the latency dashboards for that timeframe and add a note in the incident log.

maya.k: Closing loop here; thanks all :heart:
